provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `conspicis` where 1862 reads `c6nspicis`; 1962 reads `amorem` where 1862 reads `am6rem`; 1962 reads `Sanctorum tuorum exempla restaura.` where 1862 reads `sanct6rum tu6rum ex6mpla restatira.`; 1962 reads `Dominum nostrum.` where 1862 reads `D6minum.`; 1862 lower-cases sanctorum where the 1962 capitalises it; both books print the short conclusion cue, the 1862's shorter still (`Per Dominum.` against `Per Dominum nostrum.`). Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 14 October at PDF p. 850; not transcribed.

The independent registered public-domain witness is the tracked 1862 Pustet text artifact. The position is settled for the repository at src/sources/inventories/missale-romanum-1962-facsimile-rights-v1.toml, which names the seasonal orations as preexisting material and requires exactly this pairing of 103(b) with a public-domain witness.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui nos conspicis ex nostra infirmitate deficere: ad amorem tuum nos
misericorditer per Sanctorum tuorum exempla restaura. Per Dominum nostrum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
